{{ElectionsOH}}

The '''2014 Ohio State Auditor election''' was held on November 4, 2014, to elect the [[Ohio State Auditor]], concurrently with elections to the [[2014 United States House of Representatives elections in Ohio|U.S. House of Representatives]], [[2014 Ohio gubernatorial election|governor]], and other [[2014 Ohio elections|state]] and [[2014 United States elections#Local elections|local]] elections. Primary elections were held on May 6, 2014.<ref name="results">{{Cite web |title=2014 Elections Results |url=https://www.sos.state.oh.us/elections/election-results-and-data/2014-elections-results/ |access-date=December 3, 2025 |website=Ohio Secretary of State |archive-date=November 29, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201129184843/https://www.sos.state.oh.us/elections/election-results-and-data/2014-elections-results/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> A  debate was held on September 15, 2014, between all three candidates running, being the only debate held for any statewide election in Ohio in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gomez |first=Henry |date=September 15, 2014 |title=In Ohio auditor debate, incumbent Dave Yost and challenger John Patrick Carney trip over each other in attempts to claim the political high road |url=https://www.cleveland.com/open/2014/09/in_ohio_auditor_debate_incumbe.html |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rowland |first=Darrel |date=September 17, 2014 |title=Kasich, FitzGerald won't hold debates |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/politics/2014/09/17/kasich-fitzgerald-won-t-hold/23516196007/ |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=The Columbus Dispatch}}</ref>

Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] auditor [[Dave Yost]] won re-election to a second term in office against [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state representative [[John Patrick Carney]] by a margin much greater than his previous victory in [[2010 Ohio State Auditor election|2010]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Borchardt |first=Jackie |date=November 5, 2014 |title=Dave Yost defeats John Patrick Carney in Ohio auditor's race |url=https://www.cleveland.com/open/2014/11/dave_yost_defeats_john_patrick.html |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2014 |title=Republican Yost Defeats Carney In Auditor's Race |url=https://www.wyso.org/news/2014-11-04/republican-yost-defeats-carney-in-auditors-race |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=Associated Press |via=91.3 WYSO}}</ref>

== Libertarian primary ==
The [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian Party]] was not recognized as a major party in 2014 due to newly established rules regarding state recognition of political parties.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Palzer |first=Jeremy |date=November 8, 2013 |title=Libertarians file legal challenge against Ohio's new rules for minor political parties; Greens may follow suit |url=https://www.cleveland.com/open/2013/11/libertarians_file_federal_laws.html |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=cleveland.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Carr Smyth |first=Julie |date=May 1, 2014 |title=Libertarian loses appeal, remains off May ballot |url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/news/politics/elections/2014/05/01/libertarian-loses-appeal-remains-may-ballot/8561963/ |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=The Cincinnati Enquirer}}</ref> Two Libertarians running for [[2014 Ohio gubernatorial election|governor]] and [[2014 Ohio Attorney General election|attorney general]] were removed from the ballot in March 2014, which drew controversy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 7, 2014 |title=Ohio: Two Libertarians Removed From Ballot |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/08/us/ohio-two-libertarians-removed-from-ballot.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=Associated Press |via=The New York Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Vardon |first=Joe |date=March 8, 2014 |title=Libertarians angry at GOP while acknowledging faults |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/news/politics/2014/03/09/libertarians-angry-at-gop-while/23406720007/ |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=The Columbus Dispatch}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=March 12, 2014 |title=Wiped out, before a ballot is cast |url=https://www.beaconjournal.com/story/opinion/columns/2014/03/12/wiped-out-before-ballot-is/10303803007/ |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=Akron Beacon Journal |quote=Friday, Earl, his running mate, Sherry Clark, and the Libertarian candidate for attorney general, Steven Linnabary, were bounced from the May 6 primary ballot by Jon Husted, Ohio secretary of state.}}</ref> Bob Bridges, the only Libertarian running for auditor, ran a write-in primary campaign.<ref name="results" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Official Write-in Candidate Results |url=https://www.co.wood.oh.us/boe/Election_Results/2014/2014_05%20Official%20Write-in%20Candidate%20Results.pdf |access-date=December 4, 2025 |website=Wood County Board of Elections}}</ref>
